column3: The Hebrew first introduces Absalom’s beautiful sister and then says that Amnon loved her; BSB rearranges the clauses around Amnon.
The Hebrew addresses him as “son of the king”; BSB incorporates this into “you, the son of the king.”
The Hebrew explicitly mentions “bread”; BSB uses “something to eat.”
The Hebrew says that she poured out the contents before him; BSB says that she set the pan down.
The Hebrew has an unnamed subject; BSB supplies “Amnon.”
The Hebrew repeats “Amnon” and the verbs for hating and loving; BSB replaces the second name with “he” and condenses the repeated verbs.
The Hebrew says “this one” without a noun; BSB supplies “woman.”
The Hebrew describes the garment before relating her removal; BSB puts her removal first and explicitly names Amnon and Tamar.
The Hebrew repeats the description of the distinctive tunic; BSB says only “her robe.” BSB also adds “bitterly.”
The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew repeats Absalom’s name; BSB uses “he” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew explicitly names Absalom and ends with “your servant”; BSB uses “he” and “me.” BSB also supplies “just hired.”
The Hebrew says that he sent Amnon and all the king’s sons “with him”; BSB leaves this phrase implicit.
The Hebrew says “all the king’s sons”; BSB adds “other.”
